Trees: Binary Search Trees¶

Searching¶

  • A linear search of an array is very slow.

  • Binary search is faster on arrays, but

    • insertions and deletions are slow (why?)

  • Linked lists have faster insertion/deletion, but

    • only linear search is possible.

Binary Search Tree (BST)¶

  • A binary search tree (BST) is a binary tree in which each node contains a search key such that:

    • All keys less than the key in node $V$ are stored in the left subtree of $V$.

    • All keys greater than the key in node $V$ are stored in the right subtree of $V$.

  • Assumption: No duplicates

An inorder traversal will visit the nodes in sorted (increasing) order.¶

# Storage class for the binary search tree nodes of the map.
class _BSTMapNode :
    def __init__( self, key, value ):
        self.key = key
        self.value = value
        self.left = None
        self.right = None
        
    def myprnr ( self ):
        if self is not None:
            print(self.key)
            if self.left is not None:
                print(str(self.key)+"'s left:", end = "")
                self.left.myprnr ( )
            if self.right is not None:
                print(str(self.key)+"'s right:", end = "")
                self.right.myprnr ( )




class BSTMap :
    
    # Creates an empty map instance.
    def __init__( self ): 
        self._root = None 
        self._size = 0
        
    # Returns the number of entries in the map.
    def __len__( self ): 
        return self._size
    
    # Returns an iterator for traversing the keys in the map.
    def __iter__( self ):
        return _BSTMapIterator( self._root )
    

   # Determines if the map contains the given key.
    def __contains__( self, key ):
        return self._bstSearch( self._root, key ) is not None
   
    # Returns the value associated with the key.
    def valueOf( self, key ):
        node = self._bstSearch( self._root, key ) 
        assert node is not None, "Invalid map key." 
        return node.data

    # Helper method that recursively searches the tree for a target key.
    def _bstSearch( self, subtree, target ): 
        if subtree is None :
            return None
        elif target < subtree.key : # target is left of the subtree root.
            return self._bstSearch( subtree.left, target )
        elif target > subtree.key : # target is right of the subtree root.
            return self._bstSearch( subtree.right, target ) 
        else : 
            return subtree
        
    # Adds a new entry to the map or replaces the value of an existing key.
    def add( self, key, value ):
        # Find the node containing the key, if it exists.
        node = self._bstSearch( self._root, key )
        # If the key is already in the tree, update its value.
        if node is not None : 
            node.value = value 
            return False
        # Otherwise, add a new entry.
        else :
            self._root = self._bstInsert( self._root, key, value ) 
            self._size += 1
        return True
    
    # Helper method that inserts a new item, recursively.
    def _bstInsert( self, subtree, key, value ): 
        if subtree is None :
            subtree = _BSTMapNode( key, value ) 
        elif key < subtree.key :
            subtree.left = self._bstInsert( subtree.left, key, value ) 
        elif key > subtree.key :
            subtree.right = self._bstInsert( subtree.right, key, value ) 
        return subtree
    
    
    # Print the tree - added
    def prnbtree( self ):
        start = self._root
        self._root.myprnr ( )

41 has two "left" children!¶

  1. Find the logical successor, S, of the node to be deleted, N.

  2. Copy the key from node S to node N.

  3. Remove node S from the tree.

        self.left = None

    def myprnr ( self ):
        if self is not None:
            print(self.key)
            if self.left is not None:

            if self.right is not None:

class BSTMap :
    
    # Creates an empty map instance.
    def __init__( self ): 
        self._root = None 
        self._size = 0
        
    # Returns the number of entries in the map.
    def __len__( self ): 
        return self._size
    
    # Returns an iterator for traversing the keys in the map.
    def __iter__( self ):
        return _BSTMapIterator( self._root )
    

   # Determines if the map contains the given key.
    def __contains__( self, key ):
        return self._bstSearch( self._root, key ) is not None
   
    # Returns the value associated with the key.
    def valueOf( self, key ):
        node = self._bstSearch( self._root, key ) 
        assert node is not None, "Invalid map key." 
        return node.data

    # Helper method that recursively searches the tree for a target key.
    def _bstSearch( self, subtree, target ): 
        if subtree is None :
            return None
        elif target < subtree.key : # target is left of the subtree root.
            return self._bstSearch( subtree.left, target )
        elif target > subtree.key : # target is right of the subtree root.
            return self._bstSearch( subtree.right, target ) 
        else : 
            return subtree
        
    # Adds a new entry to the map or replaces the value of an existing key.
    def add( self, key, value ):
        # Find the node containing the key, if it exists.
        node = self._bstSearch( self._root, key )
        # If the key is already in the tree, update its value.
        if node is not None : 
            node.value = value 
            return False
        # Otherwise, add a new entry.
        else :
            self._root = self._bstInsert( self._root, key, value ) 
            self._size += 1
        return True
    
    # Helper method that inserts a new item, recursively.
    def _bstInsert( self, subtree, key, value ): 
        if subtree is None :
            subtree = _BSTMapNode( key, value ) 
        elif key < subtree.key :
            subtree.left = self._bstInsert( subtree.left, key, value ) 
        elif key > subtree.key :
            subtree.right = self._bstInsert( subtree.right, key, value ) 
        return subtree
    
    
    # Print the tree - added
    def prnbtree( self ):
        start = self._root
        print("root:",end='')
        self._root.myprnr ( )
        print("------")
    
    # Helper method for finding the node containing the minimum key.
    def _bstMinimum( self, subtree ): 
        if subtree is None :
            return None
        elif subtree.left is None :
            return subtree 
        else :
            return self._bstMinimum( subtree.left )
        
    # Removes the map entry associated with the given key.
    def remove( self, key ):
        assert key in self, "Invalid map key." 
        self._root = self._bstRemove( self._root, key ) 
        self._size -= 1
    
     # Helper method that removes an existing item recursively.
    def _bstRemove( self, subtree, target ): # Search for the item in the tree.
        if subtree is None : 
            return subtree
        elif target < subtree.key :
            subtree.left = self._bstRemove( subtree.left, target ) 
            return subtree
        elif target > subtree.key :
            subtree.right = self._bstRemove( subtree.right, target ) 
            return subtree
        # We found the node containing the item.
        else :
            if subtree.left is None and subtree.right is None :
                return None
            elif subtree.left is None or subtree.right is None :
                if subtree.left is not None : 
                    return subtree.left
                else :
                    return subtree.right
            else:
                successor = self._bstMinimum( subtree.right )
                subtree.key = successor.key
                subtree.value = successor.value
                subtree.right = self._bstRemove( subtree.right, successor.key ) 
                return subtree

class BSTMap :
    
    # Creates an empty map instance.
    def __init__( self ): 
        self._root = None 
        self._size = 0
        
    # Returns the number of entries in the map.
    def __len__( self ): 
        return self._size
        
   # Determines if the map contains the given key.
    def __contains__( self, key ):
        return self._bstSearch( self._root, key ) is not None
   
    # Returns the value associated with the key.
    def valueOf( self, key ):
        node = self._bstSearch( self._root, key ) 
        assert node is not None, "Invalid map key." 
        return node.data

    # Helper method that recursively searches the tree for a target key.
    def _bstSearch( self, subtree, target ): 
        if subtree is None :
            return None
        elif target < subtree.key : # target is left of the subtree root.
            return self._bstSearch( subtree.left, target )
        elif target > subtree.key : # target is right of the subtree root.
            return self._bstSearch( subtree.right, target ) 
        else : 
            return subtree
        
    # Adds a new entry to the map or replaces the value of an existing key.
    def add( self, key, value ):
        # Find the node containing the key, if it exists.
        node = self._bstSearch( self._root, key )
        # If the key is already in the tree, update its value.
        if node is not None : 
            node.value = value 
            return False
        # Otherwise, add a new entry.
        else :
            self._root = self._bstInsert( self._root, key, value ) 
            self._size += 1
        return True
    
    # Helper method that inserts a new item, recursively.
    def _bstInsert( self, subtree, key, value ): 
        if subtree is None :
            subtree = _BSTMapNode( key, value ) 
        elif key < subtree.key :
            subtree.left = self._bstInsert( subtree.left, key, value ) 
        elif key > subtree.key :
            subtree.right = self._bstInsert( subtree.right, key, value ) 
        return subtree
    
    
    # Print the tree - added
    def prnbtree( self ):
        start = self._root
        print("\n-- tree --")
        print("root:",end='')
        self._root.myprnr ( )
        print("------\n")
    
    # Helper method for finding the node containing the minimum key.
    def _bstMinimum( self, subtree ): 
        if subtree is None :
            return None
        elif subtree.left is None :
            return subtree 
        else :
            return self._bstMinimum( subtree.left )
        
    # Removes the map entry associated with the given key.
    def remove( self, key ):
        assert key in self, "Invalid map key." 
        print("..remove:",self._root.key, key)
        self._root = self._bstRemove( self._root, key ) 
        print("..remove:",self._root.key)
        self._size -= 1
    
     # Helper method that removes an existing item recursively.
    def _bstRemove( self, subtree, target ): # Search for the item in the tree.
        if subtree is None : 
            return subtree
        elif target < subtree.key :
            print("..bstRemove: looking for",target,"in:",subtree.left.key)
            subtree.left = self._bstRemove( subtree.left, target ) 
            return subtree
        elif target > subtree.key :
            print("..bstRemove: looking for",target,"in:",subtree.right.key)
            subtree.right = self._bstRemove( subtree.right, target ) 
            return subtree
        # We found the node containing the item.
        else :
            if subtree.left is None and subtree.right is None :
                print("..bstRemove:",subtree.key,"has no kids")
                return None
            elif subtree.left is None or subtree.right is None :
                print("..bstRemove:",subtree.key,"has one kid")
                if subtree.left is not None : 
                    return subtree.left
                else :
                    return subtree.right
            else:
                print("..bstRemove:",subtree.key,"has two kids")
                successor = self._bstMinimum( subtree.right )
                print("..bstRemove: successor found:", successor.key)
                print("..bstRemove:",str(subtree.key)+"'s right was",subtree.right.key)
                subtree.key = successor.key
                subtree.value = successor.value
                print("..bstRemove:",str(subtree.key)+"'s right now is",subtree.right.key)
                subtree.right = self._bstRemove( subtree.right, successor.key ) 
                print("..bstRemove:",str(subtree.key)+"'s right is",subtree.right.key)
                return subtree
